output.brief: The rejects are not caused by the new operators, and not by Arnholt resin alone or by the dryer alone. They happen only when the two combine. Arnholt resin dried in Press 5's degraded dryer (D5) runs about 10% rejects, on both shifts and for new and experienced operators alike. Arnholt on Press 7's healthy dryer runs 0.8%. Quillan on D5 runs 0.9%. The Arnholt trial passed because it ran only on Press 7. Arnholt arrives wetter (0.27–0.33% at the dryer inlet), and D5 can't dry it below the 0.20% limit. A week-42 test confirmed this: the same Arnholt lot dried in a good dryer gave 0.8% rejects, against 10.4% through D5. Second shift looks worse only because all its VX runs on Press 5. Don't put the six operators on improvement plans. Do this week: repair D5 (heater and desiccant) and restore the original alarm limit. Until D5 is verified, keep Arnholt off Press 5, or dry it in a verified dryer. Check feed-throat moisture on every VX lot. Don't drop Arnholt or move the octabins yet. Storage conditions are untested because Arnholt has only been held in the annex. I'm fairly confident, since the evidence points one way.
